apply_rules: Apply in the listed order on the RAW content (context=edit). Every "old" matches content.rendered exactly once at its turn (matches_in_live), except "replace_all" entries, which match exactly "expect_matches" times.

Edits with "spans_tags": true replace a whole <table> element: if "old" does not match the raw content exactly (raw line breaks between tags can differ), locate the single <table> element that contains "anchor" and replace that element with "new".

Every other old string sits inside one paragraph, list item or table cell and holds no HTML entity. The rendered content shows straight quotes (ש"ח, מ"ר) and no texturized characters, so raw and rendered text are expected to be identical inside a paragraph; re-check each old against the raw content right before applying.

tier 1 = sale-price alignment with the official list (conflicts, stale and unsourced sale figures); tier 2 = rent or other figures with no dated source. Applying tier 1 alone is valid (tier 2 olds do not overlap tier 1 results).
All or nothing per page: if any old does not match, write nothing. Re-fetch the page first; another session may have edited it. Data only: nothing here was applied.

Tier 2 under the CEO rule (7.10.2026): apply AFTER tier 1 (tier 1 is already live on this page), on the live content, in the listed order. Each tier-2 edit carries ceo_action (replaced = an official dated value now stands there, with its source_url; removed = number gone, sentence or cell kept; deleted = sentence, row or column gone) and ceo_note.

Tier 3 under the CEO rule (7.10.2026): listing-site rents left in the body. Apply AFTER tier 1 and tier 2 (both are live on this page), on the live content, in the listed order. ceo_action: replaced = the CBS value (table 4.9, Q2 2026) now stands there, with its source_url; removed = number gone, sentence or cell kept; deleted = sentence, row, column or paragraph gone. notes: No figure in the body conflicted per room count: the 3/4/5-room working ranges are wide enough to hold the official medians. The real conflicts are the city average 2.9M (three places) against the official all-rooms median 2,717,100, and the neighbourhood table: 12 all-rooms averages over thousands of historical deals (e.g. Gila 1,215,394, Neve Yaakov 1,144,649) sit far below the official 1-3.2026 medians by rooms and would contradict the price list directly below the lead. The rooms table and the 3/4/5 FAQ answers are rewritten to the official medians so the body says the same thing as the list (verdict CONSISTENT on those edits). Not audited as claims (illustrations or method, not market statements): the per-m2 arithmetic examples 3,200,000/80 and 2,100,000/70 (p@58456), the 'example deal check' table 2.4M / 3.6M / 5.2M / 1.85M (tr@59069..59593), the offer / listing examples 2,720,000 / 2,850,000 / 3,150,000 / 3,300,000 (p@66081), the 15% size tolerance (tr@65038), months to delivery 12-48 / 3-9 (tr@61176), counts of comparables 3-6 / 5-10, flat sizes in m2, and the population row 1,078,424 (tr@44054, not a price). Rent, per-m2, listing counts, CBS and Bank of Israel figures are outside the official list and are kept where the page names the kind of source and dates it (6.6.2026 check date, May 2026, CBS 12.3.2026, BoI 25.5.2026). The 5,500-8,500 rent range in the lead is kept as a dated rent-check summary; it is consistent with the dated listing table further down (5,684-9,442). Name mapping: 'הר חומה' in the text = official 'חומת שמואל-הר חומה'; 'קריית היובל' = official 'קרית היובל'; 'קטמונים' kept as the official name (the rent table's 'קטמון א-ו' and 'קטמון הישנה' are left untouched). Official quirk: in Pisgat Zeev the 3-room median (1,754,200) is above the 4-room median (1,666,200) in 1-3.2026; shown as published. The 4-room city median fell 9.8% in a year (3,256,800 in 10-12.2025 to 2,882,400). The rooms table keeps the page's size column as a sixth column; it may need horizontal scroll on phones. Headings 'טווח עבודה למחיר דירה' and 'מדד שוק שנבדק | ערך עבודה' are kept (no number).
